newsitem.title: CHINA: China jails two labour activists for 3-1/2 yrs.
newsitem.headline: China jails two labour activists for 3-1/2 yrs.

text.p: China has sentenced two labour activists to 3-1/2 years in prison each for conspiring to subvert the government, a human rights monitoring group in Hong Kong said on Tuesday.

The Higher People's Court in the southern boomtown of Shenzhen convicted Li Wen-ming, 28, a former magazine employee, and Guo Baosheng, 25, a former university student, last month, the Information Centre of Human Rights and Democratic Movement in China said in a statement received in Beijing.

The two men, who have been in custody since 1994, were also deprived of their political rights for two years. This means they cannot talk to foreign reporters or write for overseas publications for two years after their release from prison.
Li and Guo will be eligible for release in November and December this year, respectively.
Court officials were not immediately available for comment.
Human Rights Watch, a New York-based group, said Li was reported to be in severe pain and suffering from acute kidney damage, but has been denied access to appropriate medical care.
